messages:
marco: seeing a burst of tiny-pod Pending spikes in ap-southeast1 this morning. lots of 1-2m waits then immediate evict. this started after last night's warmpool image bump. anyone digging?

lei: i ran a quick trace, it looks like node arrives Ready but gpu-labels arrive ~40s later. scheduler gives up binding and pod churn happens.

infra-bot: alert: 12 pods pending >45s in ap-southeast1 (metric: scheduler.binding.failures).

nina: can you paste the node-init logs? curious whether cloud-init or our label agent is the slow piece.

marco: excerpt from node-init:
```
Mar 22 03:11:08 kernel: kubelet: Node registered
Mar 22 03:11:09 node-init: starting label-sync
Mar 22 03:11:51 label-sync: applied labels: gpu-type=rtx_large, gpu-count=8 (duration=42s)
Mar 22 03:11:51 kubelet: Node Ready
```

ops: ah, label-sync finishes then kubelet Ready; but scheduler sees Ready earlier in some paths due to race with cloud-provider status update. mismatch in ordering between cloud-status and kubelet internal readiness.

lei: short term fix: increase tiny-pod retry/backoff and binding wait so they don't evict on transient label arrival. long term: move label-sync earlier or block Ready until labels present.

marco: i prefer the conservative config change first to avoid customer impact. propose: bindingTimeout=120s for podClass=tiny, backoff=10s, and enable a fast label-cache lookup in scheduler.

ops: patch idea (scheduler config):
```
podClasses:
  tiny:
    bindingTimeoutSeconds: "120"
    requeueDelaySeconds: "10"
```

nina: watch out for cost/migration churn - if we keep pods pending longer we might increase egress from repeated preemptions. maybe only increase for warmpool-backed nodes or set a conditional rule by node label presence.

lei: canary plan: roll bindingTimeout to 10% for ap-southeast1 tiny class and measure pending_count, eviction_rate, and migration_egress for 1h. if good, escalate to 50%, then global.

infra-bot: created canary: /canary create config bindingTimeout-tiny ap-southeast1 10% (id=cny-4321).

marco: also adding a lightweight probe in node-init to push gpu labels ASAP (pre-label hook) is low risk and should reduce tail. i'll open an RFC for the init-order change.

ops: alternative: scheduler does a label-wait path on binding when the pod requests gpu resources: when bind fails due to missing node labels, do a short polling loop for label arrival for tiny pods before failing. that avoids pushing timeouts globally.

lei: agree, combined approach: immediate scheduler-side wait for label arrival (5-30s), plus canary bindingTimeout bump. takes less infra churn.

oncall: i've subscribed to the canary and will monitor. signal to watch: scheduler.label_waits.succeeded, scheduler.binding_retries, pending_p99. escalate if eviction_rate or network_egress rises >10%.

marco: created PR for scheduler label-wait + canary config: https://go/redux/pull/8754. attaching dashboard: https://go/redux/dashboards/sched-labels?env=ap-southeast1

nina: FYI cost note: last time pending churn hit, our cross-AZ migration egress jumped ~120GB/hr for short-lived tiny jobs. keep an eye on egress costs if we extend timeouts.

lei: thanks everyone. i'll coordinate the canary rollout and schedule a post-mortem to decide if node-init ordering change is worth the break/rollback risk.

oncall: ack, will watch for 2h and ping if any regressions.

marco: will follow up in #eng-platform once the 10% canary shows stable numbers.
